what: nec2c and NEC-5 peak-memory ladders on arrays.bowtiearray2x4 — companion to bs2-memory-ladder.json (same geometry, same rungs)
instrument: scratchpad nec_mem_ladder.py: matched-dimension decks (nec2c via nec_export anchor_deck, NEC-5 via NEC5Engine.deck), each binary under `ulimit -v 8 GB` wrapped in /usr/bin/time -v; peak = child binary max RSS; runs sequential

conditions.geometry: arrays.bowtiearray2x4, free space, 28.5 MHz, single-frequency FR
conditions.note: segment counts differ by a few segs between engines (parity coercion); dense_NxN uses each deck's own count at 16 B/entry

z_sanity: nec2c reads 212+37j across the ladder (vs bs2's mesh-stable 211+30j — the known NEC-2 reactance offset on this geometry class); NEC-5 printouts parsed OK on every rung

memory_model.nec2c: peak = dense + 3-5 MB (1.004x dense) — allocates essentially nothing but the in-core matrix
memory_model.nec5: peak -> ~1.02x dense + ~50-60 MB at large N (1.6x at small N where the fixed footprint dominates)
memory_model.bs2: peak = 1.6-2.2x dense + 300-500 MB transient (see bs2-memory-ladder.json; excess = td_all + swept chunks, momwire#318)

comparison.wall_time: NEC-5 ~12.7x faster than nec2c at 8.3k segs and within ~25% of bs2; nec2c's unblocked O(N^3) factor dominates its ladder
comparison.ceiling_8gb: nec2c ~23k segs, NEC-5 ~22.8k segs, bs2 ~15-16k basis today (~18k if momwire#318 windows td_all)
